mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates an ultra-loose monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the central bank maintains accommodative conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by >0.3pp in one month.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP growth (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) decline by more than 5% from their 12-month prior levels, it indicates a synchronized contraction in economic activity that reduces equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both decline >5% from 12-month prior
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both GDPC1 and INDPRO decline >5% from 12-month prior.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 260 indicates elevated inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to rising discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 260.

mechanism_narrative: A PAYEMS level above 140,000 thousand persons indicates a robust labor market that sustains consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 140,000.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level below 1600 thousand units indicates a contraction in the housing market that reduces construction activity and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 1600.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.1 percentage points and CPIAUCSL by more than 1.0 point in the past month signals aggressive monetary tightening amid inflation, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 1.0 point in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 1.0 point in one month.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 250 and GDP (GDPC1) remains above 18,000 billion dollars, it indicates a late-cycle expansion with inflationary pressures that triggers impending monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 250 and GDPC1 > 18000.
